source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
One CyrusOne campus in Quincy holds 36 MW of IT capacity, 60 percent of all Washington data center load on public record, yet only 2 of the state's 46 mapped facilities disclose any capacity.

The building is dense. Its 720,000 square feet of technical space against 36 MW works out to about 50 watts per square foot, and at a typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack the same load is roughly 900 racks. Those figures describe what the facility can support, not what it runs. Published specifications do not identify the tenant mix or the workload type.

For AI scaling, the relevant fact is that one campus is a large block of power in a state where almost nothing else is declared. What the numbers cannot say is whether the 36 MW is drawn today or held as headroom, whether the grid connection can carry more, or whether the operator has filed for capacity beyond what is disclosed. The suitability score of 68 lists announced expansion as its missing input, which is the same gap stated numerically.

Visibility is the real limit. With 46 mapped facilities in Washington and 2 publishing capacity, the 60 percent share is a share of disclosed load, not of the state's actual footprint. No certifications and no utility partnership details are published for this site, so nothing here speaks to how the power is contracted or delivered.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
